Twelve comments

Swan from Transatlantic Sessions

Having added “Bethany’s waltz” from an earlier Trans. Session, I fell in love with this tune by Catriona Mackay. I recorded it from the latest broadcast of the sessions (I believe they are all repeats but I missed the originals). It has driven me mad trying to work out what is tune, what is harmony and sometimes what is ornamentation. This is as close as I can get with my poor auditory equipment aka a pair of ears. Please feel free to add in corrections and/or improvements.
As a landlubber I’m guessing that LK 243 stands for the port registration of the boat she sailed in and that that port is Lerwick?

↳ Posted by onscuba on January 27th, 2010.

The Swan

Fiddlers’ Bid recorded this beautiful tune on their third album, Da Farder Ben Da Welcomer. According to the liner notes,
“The Swan is an old Fifie fishing vessel that was launched in Lerwick on 3 May 1900. The vessel has been recently restored and is used as a sail training vessel operating out of Lerwick. Catriona along with Chris and Andrew were aboard the Swan during the Cutty Sark Tall Ships Race in 1999, an experience they will never forget.”

Catriona composed the tune on this journey.

↳ Posted by Jürgen on January 30th, 2010.

Swan LK243, X:5

Better for flute

↳ Posted by Matthieu on July 4th, 2023.

The Swan LK243, X:6

I have transposed X;3 into A Major. This tune has a very large range. Some of the other versions here deal with that by changing the octave during the tune, or making other changes. For flute and whistle players, this becomes second nature when a tune goes down to the bottom string of the fiddle. I am not sure how those versions of this tune would sound.
I’m playing this on mandolin with a flute player who chose that key to be able to play the tune as composed.
in A Major the lowest note is C# and the highest C#, two octaves higher. It fits, just! It forces me u up the top E string further than I’ve played it before. All good practice!

↳ Posted by Philip W on November 5th, 2023.
